questions.q: In an `if` / `else if` / `else` chain, how many branches actually run?
options: Every branch whose condition is true runs
Only one branch ever runs -- Apex checks conditions top to bottom and stops at the first true one, or falls to the else if none are true
All branches always run regardless of their conditions
None of the branches run unless an else is present
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that only one branch ever runs: Apex checks conditions in order and stops at the first true one, skipping every other branch entirely.

questions.q: Why does putting a broader condition before a narrower one in an if/else if chain create a problem?
options: It causes a compile-time error
It makes the program run slower but otherwise behaves correctly
It silently makes the narrower branch unreachable, since any case satisfying the narrower condition already satisfies the broader one placed above it, and the code compiles fine without warning
Apex automatically reorders conditions from narrowest to broadest
questions.explain: The lesson's example shows that if `orderTotal >= 50` were checked before `orderTotal >= 100`, the more specific branch below it would never run, and this compiles and runs without any error -- it's a silent logic bug.

questions.q: What must be true about a `when else` block in an Apex `switch on` statement, per this lesson?
options: It must be the first block listed
It is required in every switch statement
If included, it must be the last block, and it acts as the catch-all equivalent to a final else
It can only be used with Integer values, never Strings
questions.explain: The lesson states the when else block is optional, acts as the catch-all, and if you include it, it must be the last block in the switch statement.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what happens after a matching `when` block runs in an Apex switch statement?
options: Execution falls through into the next when block automatically, like some other C-family languages without a break statement
The switch statement exits -- there is no fall-through between blocks in Apex
The entire program stops running
Every remaining when block also runs
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly contrasts Apex's switch with languages that fall through without a break: once a matching block runs, the Apex switch statement exits with no fall-through.

questions.q: Why is a missing `else` branch that silently does nothing considered a risky mistake, per this lesson?
options: Because Apex refuses to compile code without an else branch
Because it has no real consequence and is purely a style issue
Because when the condition is false, nothing visible happens -- no output or error -- making the missed case easy to overlook if only the true path was ever tested
Because an else branch is required for every if statement in Apex
questions.explain: The lesson notes that a missing else quietly produces no output and no error when the condition is false, which is exactly why it's easy to miss during testing if only the true case is exercised.
